title: Localization and internationalization
summary: Internationalization (i18n) is making the app ready for any language and region; localization (l10n) is adding the actual translations. Use String Catalogs, system formatters and layouts that work right-to-left.
body: **In simple words:** Never hard-code user-facing text, dates, numbers or currencies. Let the system format them for the user's language and region.

**Strings:** String Catalogs (`.xcstrings`, Xcode 15+) collect strings automatically from `Text("Hello")` and `String(localized:)`, and track what is translated. Add a **comment** to give translators context.
**Plurals:** "1 item" vs "5 items" - languages have different plural rules (Arabic has six forms). Use plural variations in the String Catalog, never `count == 1 ? "item" : "items"`.
**Formatting:** `Date.formatted()`, `number.formatted(.currency(code: "INR"))`, `Measurement`, `PersonNameComponents`. The same date prints as 13/11/2026 in India and 11/13/2026 in the US.

**Right-to-left (Arabic, Hebrew):** use leading/trailing instead of left/right; SwiftUI and Auto Layout flip automatically. Flip directional icons. Test with the "Right-to-Left Pseudolanguage" scheme option.
**Text length:** German can be 30-40% longer than English. Avoid fixed widths; test with the double-length pseudolanguage.
**Server content:** send `Accept-Language`, and decide which strings come from the server already localized.
keyPoints: i18n = make it possible; l10n = translate. Do i18n from day one.
String Catalogs with translator comments; plural variations instead of if/else.
Always use system formatters for dates, numbers, currency.
Leading/trailing layout for RTL; test with pseudolanguages.

code.caption: Localized text and formatting
code.text:
Text("Welcome back, \(user.name)")          // picked up by the String Catalog

let title = String(localized: "cart.title",
                   defaultValue: "Your cart",
                   comment: "Title of the shopping cart screen")

Text("\(count) items in cart")              // plural variants defined in the catalog

let price = 1499.0.formatted(.currency(code: "INR"))   // ₹1,499.00 in en-IN
let date = order.date.formatted(date: .abbreviated, time: .shortened)

mistakes: Concatenating translated fragments ("You have" + n + "messages") - word order differs by language.
Formatting dates with a fixed `dateFormat` string for display.
followups: **How do you test without translations?** Pseudolanguages (double length, RTL, accented) from the scheme options.
**What is `Locale` vs language?** Language = translation; locale/region = formats (dates, currency, units). A user can have English language with Indian region.
